title: Chat GPT for a specialized Engine?
author: Ravenheartcawww
selftext:
Hey guys! New to the sub, so I apologize if this is breaking any rules.  
I spent roughly two years learning some of the skills required for game dev, paid for programming help, and spent at least a few thousand hours on pixel art after work each day and on the weekends. Ultimately my career, and my debts which are very demanding just kicked my ass, and I did not succeed.  
   I’ve spent the last year struggling to accept defeat, as I really do enjoy creating things, and would like to one day make a game. I’ve considered points from both sides when it comes to the ethics of using AI for pursuits like this, and while I’ve definitely enjoyed former use of Suno, and a little bit of coding help from time to time, I don’t want to lose that “human” spark of creation.  
   I can’t find any real examples of this as I search, but I wanted to reach out and get someone’s thoughts about trying to utilize ChatGPT or Claude along with Godot (or a fork of Godot) to make a specialized engine, at about an RPG maker level of complexity, to make an interface heavy game with some basic visuals, inspired by MUDs, but brought forth in a way that is a bit more palatable to a modern audience.  
   Utilizing AI as a tool to take some of the headache away from UI layout, and managing large amounts of data (and how it interacts with other entities in the data set) is the first idea I’ve had in a year that seems like it may play out well.  
I suppose I shouldn’t post without asking something specific though:  
\-If a tool of this nature was worked on, would it help anyone else in their own pursuits?  
\-Has this already been attempted, and am I just out of the loop here?

Best of luck to all of you on your own pursuits. Don’t let the pressures of life take away your will to create. 👊

comments.author: insanetheta
comments.body: I think it’s a good idea, but probably just for yourself more than as a tool to share with others.  Using AI to build exactly the toolsets you need to work within a game engine is a more professional way to work with AI than just vibe coding every step, and largely what we’ve been doing at my studio.  We’ve created more editor tools in Unity in the last year than the previous decade combined and it’s been accelerating workflows dramatically.  Game building tools you inherit from others are harder to change and customize than Ones you vibe code exactly for your own needs.

comments.author: tabaxi_gf
comments.body: Unlikely others will use your tool, but I think it's a great idea to make something for yourself to accomplish what you want.  If you're trying to make a MUD there are plenty of starting points you could use; you could even have claude/codex write a frontend in HTML and make a backend in C++, python, javascript, whatever.  I would focus on actually making a prototype of the game and don't worry so much about the tooling and if other people will use it.  That way you can just build something small first and see if it's working for you, then make a fully developed thing when you figure out it is.

comments.author: TemporalBias
comments.body: What you are describing is is entirely possible. ChatGPT + Claude + Godot + MCP and then having the AI write custom Godot extensions for your custom engine.

comments.author: FrostyDrifter
comments.body: What you're describing sounds less like a custom engine and more like a custom authoring layer on top of Godot.

comments.author: Hot_Professional8287
comments.body:
It certainly sounds like you are out of the loop. I am currently modding Patrick Star into Bloody Roar 2 and having it recompile the emulate-able PSX ROM.

You can make anything dude.
